analyst_view.overall: Early view: Two sides level on 12 points whose games have been open: Frankfurt have conceded 20 in nine under Adi Hütter and Hoffenheim's league games have produced 33 goals. Frankfurt are without right-back Elias Baum, suspended after his yellow-red card at Paderborn, and Hoffenheim are missing several defenders, including Albian Hajdari and Valentin Gendrey, while also juggling European football.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.9 goals, already high. I lean slightly higher: Frankfurt's games average almost four goals, and both back lines are weakened, Frankfurt without Baum and Hoffenheim without Hajdari, Gendrey and Robin Hranac. Hütter's teams press aggressively, which produces chances at both ends.

corners.text: The site expects 10.2 corners. Both teams attack through the middle as much as the flanks, Frankfurt with Can Uzun and Farès Chaïbi, Hoffenheim with two strikers in Fisnik Asllani and Tim Lemperle, so I see no reason to move far from the number.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.9 cards. I lean slightly lower: Hoffenheim have been disciplined lately, with one booking at Bremen and none in the win over Schalke. Frankfurt's recent cards came in tense finishes (Baum sent off at Paderborn, Hütter booked against Hamburg), but without a derby edge this looks like an average game for bookings.

shots.text: The site has 28.3 shots, split almost evenly. Both sides take plenty of shots, and Hoffenheim's patchy finishing (one shot on target at Bremen despite more of the ball) affects accuracy more than volume. I stay with the number.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.1 on target. I lean a little higher because both defences are depleted and Frankfurt have conceded 20 goals in nine, so opponents regularly hit the target against them. Jonathan Burkardt, with two goals at Paderborn, and Younes Ebnoutalib give Frankfurt two finishers in form.
